2D isotopic lattice topologies exhibit different failure modes (brittle or ductile) when the lattice constituent material is elastic-brittle or elasto-plastic.

the fracture toughness and fracture resistance of lattice materials depend both on the lattice architecture (topology and relative density) and the constituent material (elastic or elasto-plastic) behavior.

we have developed a numerical approach for calculating fracture toughness and R-curve of lattice materials and we have unveiled the impact of lattice topologies, relative density and the constituent material behavior on toughening response of lattice materials.

, for brittle lattices, the R-curve is determined by the lattice topology and relative density, and for elasto-plastic lattices, it is also determined by the material behavior of the constituent material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the R-curves of lattice materials can be calculated using simple beam elements, and can be tailored by selecting the lattice topology and the constituent material.
the proposed numerical approach is versatile and can be used to calculate the fracture response of lattice materials with arbitrary lattice topology and constituent behavior.

, in the absence of a closed-form solution for the R-curve, a numerical approach based on the J-integral can be used to calculate the R-curves and fracture toughness for any lattice architecture, and any brittle and elasto-plastic material.
